messages:
ashley: Quick RFC follow-up — kernel priority heuristics for A100 / H100 / L4. Wanted to capture proposed fallback rules and a few open questions.

ashley: TL;DR: probe SM feature bits at startup, pick H100-optimized kernels when dp/dpx/fp8 features present, fall back to A100 kernels when H100 features missing, and route to L4 int8 paths for short-seq/low-memory cases.

ben: Do we have the exact probe order? e.g., check fp8 first or check dp/xla ops?

ashley: Probe order we sketched: 1) supports_fp8, 2) supports_dpas/dp4a/dpx-equivalents, 3) shared_mem/regs_limit, 4) max_seq. If supports_fp8+dp -> enable h100_fast_attn.

keiko: Curious about memory/occupancy tradeoffs — H100 path uses more shared mem, right? could reduce occupancy and hurt small-batch latency.

ashley: Yep. H100 kernel (our fast-attn) increases shared usage to lower per-token cycles. For tiny batches that hurts. That's why we want a small-seq heuristic: if batch*seq < threshold -> prefer l4_low_mem or a100_mm depending on feature bits.

oliver: Suggest adding an explicit policy table instead of hardcoded rules. Example config: 
```
kernel_priority:
  - h100_fast_attn
  - a100_tensor_mm
  - l4_int8_fastpath
fallback:
  - quantized_kv_cache
  - cpu_emulation
seq_routing:
  - {max_seq: 128, prefer: l4_int8_fastpath}
```
That keeps runtime simple to evaluate.

ashley: Love the table idea. Runtime loads JSON policy and evaluates machine capabilities against each entry. Simpler to test and to update.

tariq: What about probing cost? probing every worker on startup ok, but we need a safe fallback if probe fails mid-run (driver reset).

ashley: Plan: probe at worker start and cache; on driver failure detect via cuda errors and re-probe. If probe fails, fall back to the most conservative path (a100_mm or l4_int8 depending on memory). Add telemetry event on any fallback.

infra-bot: benchmark/gpu-suite: h100 median latency (batch=4, seq=512) = 12.4ms, a100 = 14.1ms, l4_int8 = 9.8ms (but quality/quant errors + higher seq cost). Baselines recorded: run_id=2026-03-18-78.

ben: Important: baseline shows l4 fastest for that config — need to ensure we route by cost+quality, not raw latency.

keiko: For quality-aware routing we need a score function: cost_weight, latency_weight, quality_penalty. Do we want it per-tenant?

ashley: Yes configurable per-tenant. Defaults: prioritize latency then cost, but enterprise tenants can force quality-first which biases away from int8 paths.

tariq: Tests/rollout items: 1) unit tests for probe logic, 2) perf harness for each kernel variant, 3) canary rollout that pins small % to new policy, 4) alert on error/fallback spikes.

oliver: Also add model-size heuristics — some kernels only safe up to hidden_dim X. Add that to capability matrix.

ashley: Decision summary: implement capability matrix + JSON policy table, probe at startup + re-probe on driver errors, add telemetry for fallbacks, add seq/batch routing heuristics, and per-tenant policy overrides. Open follow-ups: create perf benchmarks (tariq), add unit tests (ben), write rollout playbook (keiko).

ashley: Thanks — will spin up PR with config + probe code and link here when ready. :thumbsup:
